=You are a Document Data Extractor. Given extracted text from a document, organize the information into a structured JSON object.

**Output Requirements:**
- Respond with ONLY the JSON object. No explanations or other text.
- If no readable content exists, respond with: {}

**Classification (REQUIRED):**
Always include these two fields:
- content_class: "primary_document" (text-heavy document needing storage: invoices, receipts, contracts, letters) | "style_element" (logos, signatures, banners, decorative images) | "unclassified" (doesn't fit either)
- class_confidence: 0.0 to 1.0 (your confidence in the classification)

{{ (() => { const e = $('Set Default Extraction').first().json.extraction || {}; let ctx = ''; if (e.type) ctx += `Document type: ${e.type}\n`; if (e.focus_fields?.length) ctx += `Priority fields: ${e.focus_fields.join(', ')}\n`; if (e.instructions) ctx += `Instructions: ${e.instructions}\n`; return ctx ? '**Caller Context:**\n' + ctx + '\n' : ''; })() }}**Key Naming Rules:**
1. Use `snake_case` in English
2. Derive keys from visible labels (e.g., "Invoice #:" → `invoice_number`, "Date:" → `date`)
3. For unlabeled data, create descriptive `snake_case` keys
4. Prefix uncertain mappings with `uncertain_`
5. Omit keys for missing information—never invent data

parameters.content:
## Any File to JSON Converter

Turns any file a workflow receives into clean JSON: images, PDFs, spreadsheets, JSON, text documents and web pages. Call it from any workflow that handles attachments or Drive files, and get one predictable result per file.

### How it works
1. A parent workflow sends binary files, or a URL, plus an optional `extraction` object naming the fields it wants.
2. Each file becomes its own item, and a JSON Schema is built from `extraction.field_schemas`.
3. Files are routed by MIME type: images go to a vision LLM, everything else to native text extraction.
4. If fields were requested, an LLM turns the text into JSON matching them.
5. Every file returns `{status, error, data: {text, content_class, class_confidence}}`. `status` is `ok`, or `unsupported` when no route matches.
6. A step that fails (corrupt PDF, unreachable URL) fails the run, so the parent's error workflow sees it. To keep going per file, set the parent's Execute Workflow node to continue on error.

### Setup steps
- [ ] Add a **vision-capable LLM** credential to **Vision LLM**
- [ ] Add an **LLM** credential to **Text LLM** (a free tier works)
- [ ] Save and **publish**: parents run the published version
- [ ] In the parent, add an **Execute Workflow** node pointing at this workflow, passing `binary_files` and an optional `extraction`

### Customization
- Support a new MIME type in **Route by File Type**. Pick the branch by what it can decode, not by the label.
- `class_confidence` (0-1) lets the parent auto-accept, review or flag each result. See [confidence scoring](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/docs/observability-through-llm-confidence-estimate.md).

[Node-by-node docs](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/03_any-file2json-converter/workflows/mainflow.md) · Used by [smart-folder2table](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/02_smart-table-fill/workflows/smart-folder2table.json) and [inbox-attachment-organizer](https://github.com/runfish5/micro-services/blob/main/projects/n8n/04_inbox-attachment-organizer/README.md)

## Receive and split files
Defaults `extraction`, gives each attachment its own item, and builds the JSON Schema.

## Read images with a vision LLM
Normalizes the image, then extracts every visible field plus a classification.
One image per 13 s across all runs (slot in data table `vision_pacing`). A per-minute 429 waits and retries; a used-up daily quota stops the calls and returns those images `stopped`.

## Extract text by file type
Native extractors for PDF, JSON, text, CSV and Excel. URLs are fetched as markdown.

## Structure text into your fields
Runs only when the caller requested fields. Otherwise the raw text is returned.

## Return one result per file
Same shape on every path. An unknown file type returns `status: unsupported`.

nodes.name: Loop Over Images
nodes.notes: One image per pass, so each vision request is paced on its own (a caller may send several files in one run).

nodes.name: Pace Vision Requests
nodes.notes: Waits for the slot Take Vision Slot reserved: the free vision tier allows 5 requests per minute, and the slot keeps every run of this workflow together at one request per 13 s.

nodes.name: Check Vision Quota
nodes.notes: n8n data table vision_quota (model, quota_limit, resets_at, quota_id, hit_at). One row per model, written by Remember Vision Quota when the free DAILY quota is used up; cleared by the inbox organizer's /rerun_attachments.

nodes.name: Read Quota Error
nodes.notes: The LLM node keeps only "too many requests" and drops the 429 body, which is what names the quota. On a rate limit this asks the same model once more with a one-token request: while the quota is exhausted it is refused (costs nothing) and the refusal carries the quota id, limit and retry delay. Any other error only reads the model's metadata (free).

nodes.name: Read Vision Slot
nodes.notes: n8n data table vision_pacing: one row, next_request_at = the earliest time the next vision request may go out. Every run of this workflow shares it, so runs that overlap (a poll during a backfill, two polls at once) still send one request per 13 s between them. No row: requests go out unpaced.

nodes.name: Take Vision Slot
nodes.notes: Compare-and-swap: moves next_request_at 13 s past this request's slot (now, or the stored time if later), but only if the row still holds the value just read. A run that read the same value at the same moment updates nothing and reads again, so no two requests share a slot.

nodes.name: Wait Out Vision Limit
nodes.notes: A per-minute 429 got through (another workflow on the same key, or a request outside the slot): waits the delay the provider names, then takes a new slot and sends the image again.
